newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAFRICA BENCO FLOATING MINE STARTS TRIALS.
newsitem.headline: SAFRICA BENCO FLOATING MINE STARTS TRIALS.

text.p: South African firm Benco's 45 million rand Moonstar floating diamond mine has started mining trials and is expected to be in full production by May, managing director Stuart Smith said on Wednesday.
"It is all going according to plan," Smith told Reuters.
"We have finished our ore body development and we have started our trial mining into mining activities," he added
The quality of the gems being recovered was very similar to those in taken during sampling in terms of size and distribution, Smith said.
The Moonstar, a joint venture with Australia's Moonstone Diamond Corporation NL , is mining Concession 2b, which is near Port Nolloth.

The Moonstar features the latest technology in marine diamond mining. Once it is running at full capacity it is expected to operate 24 hours a day and produce up to 65,000 carats a year in Concessions 2b and 3b.
The floating mine is expected to genrate a gross annual income of around $13 million.

The deposits in the concessions were identified during a drilling programme carried out by Benco's joint venture with BHP of Australia in 1994. BHP pulled out because the finds were not large enough for it and Moonstone joined up with Benco.
